articles.title: Upgrade your at-home coffee game with these easy fixes
articles.summary: Ditch the daily Starbucks and level up your coffee skill with these upgrades that promise a smoother sip. Drip or instant? Our blind taste test and the best instant coffees. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Coffee simply tastes better at a cafe – and if you have found yourself using this sentiment to justify dropping $10 on a latte each morning, you are not alone.

It does not have to be this way. To help you upgrade your at-home coffee game, we interviewed baristas, tested 10 milk frothers, tried every model of the AeroPress coffee maker and conducted our own blind taste test pitting instant against drip.
Years ago, I was convinced that my at-home coffee setup would not be complete without dropping $1,000 on a fancy espresso machine.

That all changed after I discovered the brilliance of the moka pot. I first discovered this adorable, kettle-like coffee maker while studying in Rome and have been loyal to it ever since. I love that it creates espresso-like beverages without the four-digit price tag.

articles.title: Forget T-maxxing – the manosphere’s obsession with testosterone is just fear-maxxing | Donna Lu
articles.summary: Testosterone replacement therapy comes with serious and potentially irreversible health risks including infertility and early heart disease. Are you tired? Feeling flat and irritable? Finding it difficult to concentrate? Maybe you’re experiencing the seemingly ubiquitous symptoms of modern life.
body: For decades, testosterone has been marketed to men as a means to maximise virility. But in recent years, social media has fuelled the “T-maxxing” trend, in which men are encouraged to maximise their testosterone levels through either natural or artificial means.
Low testosterone is being blamed in the rightwing manosphere for a crisis of masculinity; global search interest in the term is up 60% from last year.

Popular podcasters such as Joe Rogan and Andrew Huberman openly talk about taking testosterone, as has the 72-year-old Robert F Kennedy Jr, who has said he uses testosterone replacement therapy as part of an “anti-ageing protocol”.

Elsewhere in the Trump administration, the US defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, announced in July that soldiers 30 and over would be tested annually to ensure they have the “right testosterone levels”.
points: Testosterone replacement therapy comes with serious and potentially irreversible health risks including infertility and early heart disease.

articles.title: It’s September. Time to put your knees away | Zoe Williams
articles.summary: From May to August, social media is awash with photos of brown knees. But summer’s almost over and they’re all starting to blur together. It’s the start of September, so time to bid adieu to the classic holiday selfie: two brown knees.
body: Everyone’s knees look the same, which is weird given the sheer variety of body shapes, and everyone’s background is mainly the same: a body of water, conceivably a mountain. There might be a cocktail to the side, but there will never be anything interesting, such as a dog, because that would dispel the serenity. It would be good if the knees were just a frame, and between them some distant, barely legible scene were playing out, such as a sword fight or a harras of many-coloured horses, but that would run counter to the vibe: “I am completely at peace and definitely not seeking out horses and lying near them for clicks.”

articles.title: Sarah Pound’s creamy, comforting store-bought roast chicken recipes
articles.summary: Using a bachelor’s handbag as a shortcut, the cookbook author shares a cheesy chicken and leek potato bake, a chicken and bacon pie and a rich baked pasta. A store-bought roast chicken is one of my favourite shortcuts because it’s ready to be shredded and made into something new.
body: Comforting and creamy, this simple and delicious traybake comes with a warning: be very careful not to eat the whole damn thing in one sitting.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the potatoes and cook for 10–12 minutes, until just tender when pierced with a knife. Drain and allow to cool slightly. Once cool enough to handle, slice into thin rounds and set aside.

Meanwhile, make the creamy chicken filling. Heat the olive oil and butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the leek and cook, stirring occasionally, for four to five minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and cook for a further minute, until fragrant. Stir in the flour and cook for a minute, then pour in the chicken stock and cook, stirring, for two or three minutes. Slowly whisk in the milk and cream until smooth. Simmer for three or four minutes, until thickened. Add the chicken and cheeses and stir until the cheeses have melted and the sauce is creamy. Season well with salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 200C fan. Grease a 25cm × 20cm baking dish.

articles.title: Guerlain 101: From Rouge G to Abeille Royale, the Products That Define the French Beauty House
articles.summary: Nearly 200 years old, Guerlain remains relevant by being obsessed with innovation. Discover Vogue's edit of the best Guerlain products, from cult-favorite lipsticks to honey-powered skincare.
body: Guerlain has been a fixture of French luxury beauty for nearly 200 years. In an industry where new brands seem to appear overnight, maintaining that kind of longevity, and staying relevant throughout, is no small feat. As you can imagine, this has meant a lot of product launches; but according to the brand not every new idea is rushed to market.

“We take our time at Guerlain, waiting until we have something truly meaningful to offer the world,” CEO Gabrielle Saint-Genis tells Vogue. “When you’re a house that has been passionate about fragrance and cosmetics for 200 years, you are obsessed with innovating.”

One area this innovation has played out is Guerlain’s work with honey. For more than 15 years, Guerlain has developed a multi-parameter selection process to identify honeys with increasingly powerful repair activities, per Dr. Frédéric Bonté, Guerlain’s director of scientific communication. The research is far more involved than simply identifying different varieties of honey: It includes studying honeybees, analyzing the composition of the honey they produce, and examining the environments in which they live.
points: Nearly 200 years old, Guerlain remains relevant by being obsessed with innovation.

articles.title: Office Hours: For Nancy Twine, Success Starts With Soul
articles.summary: Founder of Briogeo and Soulstice, Nancy Twine shares with Vogue the beauty and wellness essentials that get her mind, body, and soul ready to take on her day.
body: During her seven years in commodity sales and trading at Goldman Sachs, Nancy Twine learned a very important piece of life advice: “Just figure [it] out.” Her career since has had several arcs.

And that’s where her story begins today. If you were to meet Twine right at this very moment, she might laugh that she’s giving birth twice this month: to a baby girl (any day now!) and a new hair-care brand called Soulstice, officially available to shop today.

While sitting next to her at Sant Ambroeus in New York, Twine is as light and calm as ever, despite experiencing such pivotal life accomplishments in such quick succession. “It’s kind of cool to launch this brand while I’m this pregnant,” she says with a smile. When I ask her how she does it all, she returns to that old mantra: “I just go figure it out.”

articles.title: Asanas at Sea? The Best Places for Yoga Around the World Are Also the Most Unconventional
articles.summary: From a rocky mountainside to the middle of the ocean, explore these singular places to practice your suryanamaskars.
body: The best places for yoga are at once picturesque and contemplative, whether it be pranayama in Ladakh’s austere landscape, dhanurasana in the thick of Thailand’s jungles, or shavasana beside an Alpine lake in New Zealand. These experiences offer as much external peace as they do internal, and even long after the session and trip have ended, it's those stirring, outdoor moments that endure. They feel like they’ve stopped time and are worth going out of the way for—planned or spontaneous. And what's better than practicing your asanas in a phenomenal natural setting? With these 10 best places for yoga, grab your go-to mat and embrace your inner yogini.

The middle of the Indian Ocean is possibly the most unique spot one can find to do yoga. Practice asanas while sailing on a traditional wooden dhow at this Maldivian resort. Lux* South Ari Atoll organizes this cruise at golden hour with an instructor guiding you on Tibetan Sound Bowl therapy, breathwork, and yoga. Sip on a refreshing drink, inhale a mood-enhancing oil blend, and float on the waves as you meditate and feel your mind reset.

body: There’s something magical about fall nail designs. Maybe it’s our autumn biases (give us cozy sweater weather, apple picking, foliage, Halloween, and pre-holiday excitement over non-stop sweating and humidity any day), but these seasonal manicure trends tend to be some of our favorites.

This fall season calls upon the color palette we’ve come to associate with cooler weather, such as burgundy, chocolate brown, burnt orange, and deep earth tones. You can also expect to see metallic details and loads of rhinestones and other jeweled embellishments to dress up all of your fall manicures.

As with any nail art, the best fall nail is the one you fall in love with. But if you’re looking for a place to help spark that creativity, then you’ve come to the right spot.
